en: Muhammad ibn Bashshar and 'Abdullah ibn Hashim both narrated it to us, saying: Yahya—meaning al-Qattan—narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim—Ibn Hashim said: from 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, while Ibn Bashshar said: from the son of Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father—from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with the like of their hadith, and they both said in their hadith from Yahya: "and the likeness of the disbeliever is like the cedar tree."

Muhammad ibn Hatim and Mahmud ibn Ghaylan both narrated it to me, saying: Bishr ibn as-Sari narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Abdullah ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, except that Mahmud said in his narration from Bishr: "and the likeness of the disbeliever is like the cedar tree," whereas Ibn Hatim said: "the likeness of the hypocrite," just as Zuhayr said.

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Bishr ibn as-Sari and 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Mahdi both narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Ka'b ibn Malik, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The likeness of the believer is like the tender plant of crops, which the winds bend, knocking it down at times and straightening it at other times, until his appointed time comes to him; and the likeness of the hypocrite is like the firmly rooted cedar tree which is affected by nothing until it is uprooted all at once."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Muhammad ibn Bishr both narrated to us: Zakariyya ibn Abi Za'idah narrated to us, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim: The son of Ka'b ibn Malik narrated to me, from his father, Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The likeness of the believer is like the tender shoot of crops, which the wind bends, knocking it down at times and straightening it at other times, until it withers; and the likeness of the disbeliever is like the cedar tree standing firm on its root, which nothing bends, until it is uprooted all at once."

Muhammad ibn Rafi' and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us from 'Abd ar-Razzaq: Ma'mar narrated to us, from az-Zuhri with this chain of narration, except that in the hadith of 'Abd ar-Razzaq, in place of his words "bends it", it has "blows it over".

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from az-Zuhri, from Sa'id, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The likeness of the believer is like that of crops: the wind continues to bend it, and afflictions continue to strike the believer; and the likeness of the hypocrite is like that of the cedar tree: it does not shake until it is cut down completely."

Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ar-Ruzzi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Wahhab ibn 'Ata' reported to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, with the meaning of their hadith.

'Asim ibn an-Nadr at-Taymi narrated to us: Mu'tamir narrated to us, saying: I heard my father: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas ibn Malik, that he narrated from the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him: "Indeed, when a disbeliever performs a good deed, he is fed a portion of worldly provision because of it; but as for the believer, Allah stores up his good deeds for him in the Hereafter and grants him provision in this world according to his obedience."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to us—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hammam ibn Yahya reported to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Indeed, Allah does not wrong a believer regarding a good deed: he is given provision for it in this world and rewarded for it in the Hereafter. As for the disbeliever, he is fed for the good deeds he did for the sake of Allah in this world, until when he arrives in the Hereafter, he has no good deed left for which to be rewarded."

'Amr an-Naqid narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Hammad ibn Salamah reported to us, from Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "The most pampered person of the worldly life among the people of the Fire will be brought on the Day of Resurrection and dipped once into the Fire, then it will be said: 'O son of Adam, did you ever see any good? Did any bliss ever come to you?' He will say: 'No, by Allah, my Lord.' And the most miserable person in the worldly life among the people of Paradise will be brought and dipped once into Paradise, then it will be said to him: 'O son of Adam, did you ever see any misery? Did any hardship ever come to you?' He will say: 'No, by Allah, my Lord, no misery ever came to me, and I never saw any hardship.'"

Zuhayr ibn Harb and 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to me—and the wording is Zuhayr's—they said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that a man said: "O Messenger of Allah, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "Is not the One Who made him walk on his two legs in the worldly life capable of making him walk on his face on the Day of Resurrection?" Qatadah said: "Yes indeed, by the Might of our Lord!"

'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Rawh ibn 'Ubadah narrated to us; (and a different chain) 'Amr ibn Zurarah narrated to me: 'Abd al-Wahhab—meaning Ibn 'Ata'—reported to us, both from Sa'id ibn Abi 'Arubah, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it, except that he said: "So it will be said to him: 'You have lied; you were asked for what was easier than that.'"

'Ubaydullah ibn 'Umar al-Qawariri, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—Ishaq said: reported to us, while the others said: Mu'adh ibn Hisham narrated to us: My father narrated to us, from Qatadah: Anas ibn Malik narrated to us that the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "It will be said to the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection: 'What do you think, if you had the earth full of gold, would you ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' So it will be said to him: 'You were asked for what was easier than that.'"

Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated it to us: Muhammad—meaning Ibn Ja'far—narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik narrate from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it, except for his words: "and that I would not admit you into the Fire," for he did not mention it.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Abu 'Imran al-Jawni, from Anas ibn Malik, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, who said: "Allah, Blessed and Exalted, will say to the person with the lightest punishment among the people of the Fire: 'If you had the worldly life and all that is in it, would you ransom yourself with it?' He will say: 'Yes.' He will say: 'I wanted from you what was easier than this, while you were still in the loins of Adam: that you not associate anything with Me'—I think he said—'and that I would not admit you into the Fire; but you insisted on nothing except polytheism.'"

'Ubaydullah ibn Sa'id narrated to me: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman as-Sulami, who said: 'Abdullah ibn Qays said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "No one is more patient over harm that he hears than Allah the Exalted: indeed, they assign partners to Him and assign to Him a son, yet despite that He provides for them, grants them well-being, and bestows upon them."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah and Abu Usamah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman as-Sulami, from Abu Musa, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "No one is more patient over harm that He hears than Allah, Mighty and Majestic: indeed, partners are associated with Him and a son is attributed to Him, yet He grants them well-being and provides for them." Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Numayr and Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj both narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us: Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated to us, from Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman as-Sulami, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of it, except for his words: "and a son is attributed to Him," for he did not mention it.

Musa ibn Quraysh at-Tamimi narrated to us: Ishaq ibn Bakr ibn Mudar narrated to us: My father narrated to me: Ja'far ibn Rabi'ah narrated to us, from 'Irak ibn Malik, from 'Ubaydullah ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Indeed, the moon split during the time of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far and Abu Dawud narrated to us; (and a different chain) Ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id, Muhammad ibn Ja'far, and Abu Dawud all narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The moon split into two parts. And in the hadith of Abu Dawud: The moon split during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and 'Abd ibn Humayd both narrated to me, saying: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us: Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, that the people of Makkah asked the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, to show them a sign, so he showed them the splitting of the moon twice. And Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated it to me: 'Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar reported to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, with the meaning of the hadith of Shayban.

Bishr ibn Khalid narrated it to me: Muhammad ibn Ja'far reported to us; (and a different chain) Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us: Ibn Abi 'Adi narrated to us, both from Shu'bah with the chain of Ibn Mu'adh from Shu'bah, similar to his hadith, except that in the hadith of Ibn Abi 'Adi: so he said: "Bear witness! Bear witness!"

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Umar, from the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, the like of that.

'Ubaydullah ibn Mu'adh al-'Anbari narrated to us: My father narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The moon split during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, into two pieces: one piece was behind the mountain and one piece was above the mountain, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "O Allah, bear witness!"

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim all narrated to us from Abu Mu'awiyah; (and a different chain) 'Umar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us: My father narrated to us, both from al-A'mash; (and a different chain) Minjab ibn al-Harith at-Tamimi narrated to us—and the wording is his: Ibn Mushir reported to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: While we were with the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, at Mina, the moon suddenly split into two halves: one half was behind the mountain and one half was below it, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said to us: "Bear witness!"

'Amr an-Naqid and Zuhayr ibn Harb both narrated to us: Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, from Abu Ma'mar, from 'Abdullah, who said: The moon split during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, into two parts, so the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said: "Bear witness!"

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us; (and a different chain) Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us—and the wording is his: Ghundar narrated to us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from 'Azrah, from al-Hasan al-'Urani, from Yahya ibn al-Jazzar, from 'Abd ar-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b regarding the words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: {"And We will surely let them taste the nearer punishment before the greater punishment"}: He said: The tribulations of this worldly life, the Romans, the violent seizure, or the smoke—Shu'bah was the one who doubted whether it was the violent seizure or the smoke.
Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us: Waki' narrated to us: Al-A'mash narrated to us with this chain of narration, the like of it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu ad-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abdullah, who said: Five things have already passed: the smoke, the inevitable punishment, the Romans, the violent seizure, and the moon.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah and Waki' narrated to us; (and a different chain) Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to me: Waki' reported to us; (and a different chain) 'Uthman ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Jarir narrated to us, all of them from al-A'mash; (and a different chain) Yahya ibn Yahya and Abu Kurayb narrated to us—and the wording is Yahya's—they said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Muslim ibn Subayh, from Masruq, who said: A man came to 'Abdullah and said: "I left in the mosque a man interpreting the Quran according to his own opinion, interpreting this verse: {'The Day that the sky will produce a visible smoke'}; he said: 'A smoke will come upon the people on the Day of Resurrection and seize their breaths until they catch from it something like a cold.'" 'Abdullah said: "Whoever has knowledge should speak according to it, and whoever does not know should say: 'Allah knows best,' for indeed it is part of a man's understanding to say about that of which he has no knowledge: 'Allah knows best.' That was only because when Quraysh disobeyed the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, he prayed against them for years like the years of Yusuf, so they were afflicted with drought and hardship until a man would look at the sky and see between himself and it something like smoke due to exhaustion, and until they ate bones. Then a man came to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, seek forgiveness from Allah for Mudar, for they have perished.' He said: 'For Mudar? You are indeed daring!' He said: So he prayed to Allah for them, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {'Indeed, We will remove the torment a little; indeed, you will return [to disbelief]'}. He said: So rain was sent upon them, and when ease reached them, they returned to what they had been doing. He said: So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: {'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, covering the people; this is a painful torment'}, and: {'The Day We will seize them with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution'}—meaning the Day of Badr."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim reported to us: Jarir reported to us, from Mansur, from Abu ad-Duha, from Masruq, who said: We were sitting with 'Abdullah while he was reclining among us, when a man came to him and said: "O Abu 'Abd ar-Rahman, indeed a story-teller at the gates of Kindah is reciting stories and claims that the sign of the smoke will come and seize the breaths of the disbelievers, while it will afflict the believers only like a cold." 'Abdullah sat up angrily and said: "O people, fear Allah! Whoever among you knows something, let him speak according to what he knows, and whoever does not know, let him say: 'Allah knows best,' for indeed it is more knowledgeable for one of you to say about that which he does not know: 'Allah knows best.' Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said to His Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him: {'Say, "I do not ask you for it any reward, and I am not of the pretentious"'}. Indeed, when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, saw the turning away of the people, he said: 'O Allah, seven years like the seven of Yusuf.' So they were seized by a year that devastated everything until they ate skins and dead animals out of hunger, and one of them would look up at the sky and see something like smoke. Then Abu Sufyan came to him and said: 'O Muhammad, you came commanding obedience to Allah and keeping ties of kinship, and indeed your people have perished, so supplicate to Allah for them.' Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: {'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke, covering the people; this is a painful torment'}, up to His words: {'indeed, you will return [to disbelief]'}. He said: 'Will the punishment of the Hereafter be removed?' {'The Day We will seize them with the greatest seizure; indeed, We will take retribution'}—and the greatest seizure was the Day of Badr. And the sign of the smoke, the violent seizure, the inevitable punishment, and the sign of the Romans have already passed."
